references.text: Here incense is mentioned among the gifts the Israelites were to bring to the sanctuary, as preparation for the incense mixture described in Exodus 30:34.
Describes how Aaron was to burn fragrant incense on the altar of incense every morning and evening, which is the purpose of the incense described in verse 34.
Bezalel made the holy anointing oil and the pure fragrant incense according to the art of the perfumer, fulfilling the command given in Exodus 30:34.
The grain offering was to have pure frankincense (levona) on it, the same ingredient mentioned in the incense mixture.
On the Day of Atonement, the high priest was to bring incense into the Most Holy Place, showing the holy use of the incense from Exodus 30:34.
Aaron used incense to make atonement for the people during a plague, demonstrating the atoning function of the incense.
David's prayer is compared to incense rising before the Lord's presence, a poetic reference to the temple service incense.
Mentions incense and myrrh in connection with fragrance, ingredients linked to holy incense.
The prophecy that frankincense (levona) will be brought from Sheba, pointing back to the significance of incense in worship.
In Revelation, the incense represents the prayers of the saints, building on Old Testament symbolism from the tabernacle service.
An angel with a golden censer burns incense together with the prayers of the saints at the altar, linking the incense to intercession and worship.
Both verses describe the specific ingredients for the holy anointing oil and incense to be used in God's service.
